content:
I want to advertise my new API design in Representation.Induced #41808. It seals off IndV.mk and ind so that simpler @[simp] lemmas are able to work around IndV.mk instead of unfolding things down to earth everytime.

Let me make some remark on the motivation first. Initially, I found it painful when working with inductions from subgroups in the development of Hecke because whenever you apply simp with a ind in you goal, your goal will be typically like

**⊢** Coinvariants.lift (tprod (MonoidHom.comp (leftRegular k G) φ) σ) (TensorProduct.lift (((Finsupp.lift (W →ₗ[k] V) k G) fun h ↦ ρ h⁻¹ ∘ₗ f.toLinearMap) ∘ₗ ↑(MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv k))) ⋯ ∘ₗ Coinvariants.map (tprod (MonoidHom.comp (leftRegular k G) φ) σ) (tprod (MonoidHom.comp (leftRegular k G) φ) σ) { toLinearMap := LinearMap.rTensor W (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainLinearMap k k fun x ↦ x * g⁻¹), isIntertwining' := ⋯ } = ρ g ∘ₗ Coinvariants.lift (tprod (MonoidHom.comp (leftRegular k G) φ) σ) (TensorProduct.lift (((Finsupp.lift (W →ₗ[k] V) k G) fun h ↦ ρ h⁻¹ ∘ₗ f.toLinearMap) ∘ₗ ↑(MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv k))) ⋯

At that time I proposed adding some rewrite lemmas (without fixing the simp behaviour) and I thought I could seal things off in the induction from subgroup (a special case of ind) API. But recently I realized that I will have to redo such things around Jacquet module, which is defined via coinvariants (another special case of ind). This isn't fun, so why not just fix ind once for all? These lead to following proposal, which should be much better than my previous ad hoc one:

I addressed the above issue by making IndV.mk a def and adding a new core defIndV.lift:

  1. Making IndV.mk a def will allow the desired new API lemmas to have the desired @[simp] behaviour (previously simp would unfold IndV.mk immediately, so @[simp] would not even invoke these lemmas).

  2. IndV.lift, which is a def, gives a way to construct a linear map from a compatible family of linear maps on elementary generators. It unifies the previous constructions in both ind and coinvariantsTensorInd. Moreover, it turns out a single @[simp] lemma IndV.lift_apply_IndVMk is good enough while previously we had the annoying @[simps] above ind unfolding several linear algebra layers at once. We then make ind simply an abbrev aboveIndV.lift.

This is really an important PR for me and I will do my best to get it merged. Any comments are welcome!

I actually never quite agreed with the setup of Coinvariants and Induced, I think if we seal everything (which is what we're currently doing), then it's only gonna be either we duplicate every declaration about the old definitions (e.g Coinvariants and quotients of submodule) or it's gonna get more and more confusing. I would suggest if we only seal the "important" definitions and keep all the others transparent, the situation would be a lot better

Edison Xie said:

I would suggest if we only seal the "important" definitions and keep all the others transparent, the situation would be a lot better

This is exactly what I am doing: now only IndV.mk and IndV.lift are def's and the others are all abbrev's including the new ind indMap (previously they are def's)! In particular, IndV remains an abbrev so that we don't need to duplicate instance like AddCommGroup
Also these two together capture the generators and relations so mathematically this should be minimal number of def's. API lemmas are built around the two.
